[Small-cap stocks](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/best-long-term-investments#small-cap-stocks). **Who are they good for?**If you’re going to [buy individual growth stocks](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/how-to-invest-in-stocks/), you’ll want to analyze the company carefully, and that can take a lot of time. **Overview:**[Investing in real estate](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/how-to-invest-in-real-estate/) has long been considered one of the best long-term investments, in part because you can borrow the bank’s money for most of the investment and then pay it back over time. Small-cap stocks are often also [high-growth stocks](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/best-performing-stocks/), but not always. **Rewards:** The potential reward on a robo-advisor account also varies based on the investments and can range from very high if you own mostly stock funds to low if you hold safer assets such as cash in a [high-yield savings account](https://www.bankrate.com/banking/savings/best-high-yield-interests-savings-accounts/). By focusing on the long term — [committing not to sell your investments as the market dips](https://www.bankrate.com/investing/timing-the-stock-market/) — you’ll be able to avoid the short-term noise that derails many investors.

We’ll start with something simple, as high-yield savings accounts represent a logical progression from something you should be doing with your money on a routine basis to an investment that makes your funds work for you. No investment is completely without risk, even government bonds, but if you’re looking for the safest of safe bets for your funds then high-yield savings accounts are for you. High-yield savings accounts also offer a lot of flexibility, so if you’re looking to use your money as an investment for a specific goal, for example, a deposit on a house, this would be a good choice for your funds too. Corporate bond funds offer many of the same advantages as government bonds, namely that they represent a safe and long-term investment that will provide a modest amount of money as income over a set period. Bonds and stock funds, investments that come in the form of real estate or savings accounts—there’s a lot of choice on offer if you want to put your money into an investment portfolio.
